title: Hill-Climbing Skills: Improve Agents Without Changing the Model — Shubhankar Srivastava, Browserbase
talk_summary: Browserbase describes an 'auto research' loop where a doer agent attempts a task and a teacher agent reads its traces and appends learnings to a persistent strategy.md, iterating until a reusable skill.md converges. They report large cost/latency savings on repeat runs and argue the same loop applies to coding agents that currently relearn repo conventions every run.

takeaways.technique: Teacher/doer trace-distillation loop producing a persistent skill file
takeaways.what_they_do: A doer agent executes the task; a teacher agent reads the run's traces/screenshots/logs and appends concrete learnings to a strategy.md that is injected into the next iteration, converging into a portable skill.md.
takeaways.numbers: Google Flights: $12 -> $3 (~4x); OpenTable: $6.22 -> $0.51, 189s -> 27s; up to 16x cheaper cited

takeaways.technique: Verifiable outcome + replayable environment as preconditions
takeaways.what_they_do: They only run the hill-climbing loop where there is a quantifiable pass/fail metric and a replayable environment; they explicitly say knowledge work with human-in-loop is hard to replay.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the two conditions that are required is that a you should have a replayable environment ... b you should have some sort of verifiable outcome

takeaways.technique: Cheaper model, more iterations beats expensive model, fewer iterations
takeaways.what_they_do: They eval'd running a cheaper model for more loop iterations vs an expensive model for fewer, and found comparable results at lower total cost; loop cost is amortized across future runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can get the same job done by throwing sonnet larger number of iterations but still cheaper overall
takeaways.numbers: one auto browse loop ~$30-40, up to $100 for complex tasks

takeaways.technique: Failure-triggered healing loop instead of continuous re-research
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than re-running the expensive loop on a schedule, they trigger a healing auto-research run only on production failure, which produces a PR to a human and updates the skill; optionally cheap periodic sample runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as soon as we run into any production failure, we run an auto research loop to see what went wrong to heal it, create a pull request

takeaways.technique: Security reviewer agent gating generated skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Generated skills are run against a security reviewer agent before publishing, plus infra-layer URL/action restrictions, to prevent prompt injection from being baked into learned skills.

takeaways.technique: Portable markdown skill artifact injected per iteration
takeaways.what_they_do: The accumulated learnings live in a plain markdown file injected into the prompt each iteration, kept small and portable across agents/SDKs rather than bloating context with full history.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It is essentially a skill. It is a portable artifact you can use in any agent or any SDK.
